To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
histologic grade and CD44std are independent predictors of axillary node invasion in early breast cancer.

histologic grade 2, Ki67 < 10% and CD44std positivity are associated with the absence of axillary lymph node involvement, whereas histologic grade 1, Ki67 > 10% and/or CD44std negativity are not, but are rather indicative of the presence of nodal metastasis in small (≤2 cm) unifocal breast carcinomas.
histologic grade 2 or 3 and CD 44std negativity were independent predictors of nodally positive disease in patients with early breast cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of patients with small, node-positive breast cancer who could be treated with breast-conserving surgery alone, and with the identification of those who would need axillary dissection as well.
the identification of the patients with T1 breast cancers who can safely be spared lymphadenectomy.

the identification of factors that could be used as predictors of nodal metastasis, with the ultimate goal of avoiding lymphadenectomy in patients with small breast cancer and negative axillary nodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the axilla should be considered as a potential site of disease dissemination in all early breast cancer patients.
the axilla should be explored in any case, and the decision to proceed to axillary lymphadenectomy should not be made on the basis of the results of any of the tests currently available.
, at least for the time being, sentinel node biopsy is the only reliable means for predicting the absence of axillary node invasion in early breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although histologic grade and CD44 are independent predictors of nodality in small breast cancers, their combination does not allow to exclude axillary nodal invasion in any case.
, in patients with early breast cancers, histologic grade and CD44std are the most important factors in the decision to perform lymphadenectomy.

the presence of histologic grade 2 and CD44std positivity, in addition to the absence of histologic grade3, could identify a subgroup of small breast cancers in which the axilla would be spared from surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of nodular metastases in the axilla, breast cancers 2 cm or smaller in diameter can be considered as being of low metastatic potential.

histologic grade and CD44std status should be considered in clinical decision-making, especially in the context of sentinel node mapping, which is becoming a widely accepted alternative to axillary lymphadenectomy in the treatment of breast cancer.
the absence of nodality in early breast cancer is not a predictable event.
